snippet.description:
👞 The Story: Fieldin Culbreth and the Infamous Gray Shoes
In 2015, veteran MLB umpire Fieldin Culbreth was fined by Major League Baseball—not for a bad call, but for wearing the wrong color shoes during a nationally televised game.

What went wrong?
MLB has a strict uniform policy for umpires: black pants, black shirts, and black shoes—no exceptions.
During a Sunday Night Baseball game between the Los Angeles Angels and Boston Red Sox (May 31, 2015), Culbreth wore gray New Balance sneakers instead of regulation black shoes.
The shoes were part of a personal comfort choice (he’d worn similar gray shoes in spring training), but they violated MLB’s official on-field dress code.
The fallout:
MLB fined him an undisclosed amount (rumored to be a few thousand dollars).
More significantly, he was removed from working the next scheduled postseason as a disciplinary measure—though he later returned to playoff duty in 2016.
The incident went viral, with fans joking that he’d committed “the ultimate fashion foul” in baseball.
Why such a big deal?
MLB enforces uniformity to maintain professionalism and neutrality. Umpires are meant to be “seen but not noticed”—and non-regulation gear breaks that illusion.

Ironically, many fans and players defended Culbreth, arguing that comfort matters during 9+ hour days on the field—and that the punishment seemed excessive for a footwear faux pas.

So yes: An MLB umpire really was fined—and benched from the playoffs—for wearing gray shoes.
